dashboard.sablelife.laser_help:
Charge then fire a beam. Fixed follows the marked face; tracking follows a visible target. Damage is per pulse and respects armor. External walls stop the beam. Turning the trigger off cancels the cast. Interval is the pause after a burst. Fixed mode sweeps across the configured angle; 0 disables sweeping.
Negative sweep angle reverses sweep direction. 0 keeps a fixed beam. Block breaking defaults Off. Whole line clears breakable centerline blocks immediately during firing. Cut forward starts at the first obstruction and advances at the configured blocks/s; speed does not extend firing time. Own connected body is skipped; unbreakable/protected blocks and unloaded terrain stop the cut. Charging and Preview never destroy blocks.
dashboard.sablelife.sequence_help: Each step emits one channel or waits. Use sequence-controlled wireless channel modes. A short input pulse runs the full sequence unless Stop on low is enabled. Reset stops immediately; a held one-shot input cannot restart until a new pulse.

sequence.sablelife.channel_help: Choose an existing, enabled channel with frequency items and sequence-controlled mode. This channel currently cannot emit sequence signals.

dashboard.sablelife.pull_help: Destination = marked face + outward offset; follows the limb. Warning sphere stays fixed for this cast. Leave it before activation to dodge. Later entrants are not captured; leaving the sphere or hiding behind a wall (LOS On) releases you. Sideways movement is preserved. No teleport or direct damage. At target uses the nearest eligible target in the search range as the fixed warning/pull center. Stopping distance is the radius around the pull center where attraction brakes/stops, not the target detection range. Defaults: beacon activate warning / beacon ambient pulling.

dashboard.sablelife.redstone_help: Items in the red/blue slots directly set the external wireless frequency. Leave them empty for Mark only. Marked-face and wireless outputs can run together. Six faces powers the marked block's neighbors. Selected surface supplies the marked block from that face. Reverse signal defaults Off. On swaps zero and the configured strength for both marked and external outputs. Hold: idle high, triggered low. Pulse: idle high, low for the pulse duration, then high again. Disabled, invalid, dormant or master Off always outputs zero. Outputs to this core's Wireless channel; 0 disables it. Enable the channel and select Sequence / internal. Uses strength, Hold/Pulse and inversion. No Mark or frequency items required; all three destinations can work together. Highest strength wins across producers. Use different input/output channels to avoid self-latching.

dashboard.sablelife.quake_help: Detection radius finds the target whose feet become the frozen origin. Wave length / effect radius controls the attack size independently. Whole area rises simultaneously; wave speed and width do not apply.
dashboard.sablelife.trigger_internal_hel: Triggered by a core internal wireless channel, including normal internal channels and Sequence / internal output. Repeating is controlled by the channel or sequence settings.
dashboard.sablelife.laser_tracking_help: Target only. 1 updates every tick; 0.1 updates every 10 ticks (0.5 s). Fire starts at the last advertised warning point.
dashboard.sablelife.target_multiple_help: Target mode only: single selects nearest; multiple selects up to 64 eligible targets. Lasers warn and track each target independently; crossing beams damage each victim once per hit interval.
dashboard.sablelife.laser_follow_help: Target only. The firing aim point moves toward the target by this distance each tick; 0.1 = 2 blocks/s. Running faster than the aim point can evade the beam. No snap at firing start.
dashboard.sablelife.homing_help: Deploy from Mark, charge, then lock targets. Single: all missiles pursue one target. Multiple: distribute missiles among targets. Higher tracking strength turns faster; speed and hitbox also affect hits.
core.sablelife.lifeAttacks_help: Allow damage from other Sable Life creatures. Own attacks always remain harmless. Player attacks are unaffected.
dashboard.sablelife.target_help: All includes players, other mobs (including added mods), and other active Sable Life creatures. Own creature is excluded. Targeting does not override the victim core’s damage immunity.

core.sablelife.death_help: Cosmetic effects play once when health reaches zero, before delayed breakup. Duration 0 uses the particle's natural lifetime. Preview does not kill the creature.
core.sablelife.pattern_help: Choose the particle layout. Left click: next; right click: previous. Spread controls its size.
core.sablelife.vanish_help: Particles play at disappearing blocks after death delay, up to 16 locations per cleanup tick. Sound plays once. Preview uses the core position without removing blocks.
dashboard.sablelife.description_linear_m: Moves the whole connected machine from a marked point. Teleport after charging, or Travel with mandatory terrain checks.
dashboard.sablelife.linear_help: Angles are relative to the marked direction: positive horizontal turns right, positive vertical turns up. Teleport always checks the destination. Travel always checks terrain and stops at the last safe position. Full limb bounds are checked, so narrow gaps may be rejected. Toward target selects the nearest eligible target within search range, fixes its center at charge start and stops N blocks before it, measured from the marked movement point. Distance at or below N causes no movement. Target mode replaces fixed distance, face direction and angle offsets; it does not rotate the body. Teleport/Travel and existing obstruction rules still apply. Creative players can be included. Use target height defaults Off, keeping displacement horizontal; On uses the recorded target height for a 3D path. Force movement defaults Off. On skips terrain/body collision prechecks. Travel advances from frozen starting positions so contact pushback cannot erase progress. Destination chunks and world bounds still apply. Terrain is not destroyed; normal physics still applies after movement.
dashboard.sablelife.move_runtime_blocked: Movement blocked: terrain, border or unloaded area
dashboard.sablelife.flame_visual_help: Particle chooses the spray appearance and per-type size/lifetime; 0 lifetime covers the path. Effects apply on successful hits, subject to the damage interval. Damage and Burn remain separate; particles do not change the hitbox.

commands.sablelife.conditional_note: Conditional: previous row must succeed in this pass.
commands.sablelife.completion_help: Tab: complete / cycle candidates; Shift+Tab: previous; arrows or mouse: select.
dashboard.sablelife.arena_death_note: Kills nearby survival players when the countdown ends.
dashboard.sablelife.arena_force_return_n: Immediately returns the creature to center with full HP; overrides player punishment.
dashboard.sablelife.arena_countdown_help: Starts when the creature leaves the arena. Each nearby survival player gets a full countdown. Returning inside cancels it; player death is optional.
dashboard.sablelife.particle_mark_help: Area and point marks are saved separately. Area needs two points on one limb; other patterns share one marked face. Sneak-right-click air clears only the current mark mode.
dashboard.sablelife.particle_pattern_hel: Area uses its two-mark box; other patterns use a marked face origin. Start distance shifts the whole pattern along Direction; Ring lies perpendicular to Direction. Random/Even controls placement; density is particles per type. Sphere can fill its interior or surface. Ring height 0 keeps one ring; positive height extends a hollow cylinder along the selected direction. Density is shared over the cylinder surface, not multiplied per layer. Outward/inward propagation moves radially around each cross-section.
dashboard.sablelife.particle_spray_help: Spray births particles at the origin and moves them at the configured speed to Length. Lifetime 0 covers the full journey; a shorter custom lifetime cuts it off. Native friction and gravity do not shorten the path.

sound_timeline.sablelife.open_help: Open the sound timeline: multiple sounds with independent start time, pitch, volume and range. MC/OGG tools are inside.
sound_timeline.sablelife.library_help: Left-click selects; double-click listens; right-click adds a layer. Duplicate sounds are allowed.
sound_timeline.sablelife.property_help: Times are relative to this event. Start 0–600s, pitch 0.5–2, volume 0–4, range 1–256 blocks.
sound_timeline.sablelife.duration_help: 0 plays naturally (BGM loops). A positive limit stops this layer at that time; fading happens within the limit. Dashed tails indicate unknown natural length.
sound_timeline.sablelife.natural: Natural length / BGM loop; timeline tail is symbolic.
sound_timeline.sablelife.cutoff: Ends at the configured playback limit.
dashboard.sablelife.melee_hit_limit_help: 0 = unlimited hits, still limited by Interval. Positive values cap successful hits per target during this continuous trigger window. Leaving/re-entering the area does not reset counts. Signal off, disable or reload starts a new window.
dashboard.sablelife.melee_offset_help: The first marked face defines forward. Positive horizontal turns right; positive vertical turns up in that face-relative plane. Angles rotate the entire box around its center and steer Start distance. The box keeps its size and follows the limb; Preview uses the same geometry.
dashboard.sablelife.melee_help: Damage and effects apply on successful contact. Interval is per target and per module. The hit cap is per continuous activation; 0 is unlimited.
core.sablelife.defense_note: Defaults 100 / 80% / 1s: 200 incoming DPS gives 50% reduction (~100 DPS); 1,000 gives 80% (~200 DPS). Steady rates after the window fills, not a hard damage cap.
core.sablelife.defense_help: Default Off. Threshold 0.1–1,000,000 HP/s; cap 0–100%; window 0.1–10s. Above the threshold, reduction rises with incoming DPS. The proposed hit is included; rejected or fully blocked hits do not count. Healing does not count. Changing these settings resets the rolling window.
core.sablelife.defenseThreshold_help: The incoming DPS at which protection begins, after armor. Lower = earlier/stronger protection; higher = more damage allowed. It is not a per-hit cap. At 200 sustained DPS with threshold 100, target reduction is 50%, unless limited by Maximum reduction.
core.sablelife.defenseMaximum_help: The highest adaptive reduction allowed, not a constant reduction. 0 = no adaptive mitigation. 80% leaves at least 20% of incoming damage: 1,000 sustained DPS can still deal about 200 DPS. Thus the DPS threshold is not a hard damage cap.
core.sablelife.defenseWindow_help: DPS = damage in the last N seconds / N. Short windows react more strongly to brief bursts and forget them sooner; long windows need more accumulated damage and retain it longer. 100 damage in a 1s window = 100 DPS; in 0.5s = 200 DPS. This is a measuring window, not an immunity duration.
manual.sablelife.title: Operating manual
manual.sablelife.schema_note:
Values below come from the module definitions, not your saved configuration. Time fields use seconds; other units follow their labels.

Color rows have an RGB button: On disables presets and expands three 0–255 channels; Off collapses them and restores the preset, retaining custom values.

Some fields appear only in applicable modes. Sound layers are edited in the sound timeline.
manual.sablelife.getting_started.usage: Use the Heart to inspect and activate a connected creature. Creative authoring uses the dashboard; Release, available in the dashboard and on every Core settings page, returns the creature to a dormant editing state without dismantling its build.
manual.sablelife.getting_started.setting:
Empty-hand right-click: inspect; in creative mode it reopens the last editor for this core (Virtual modules on first use).

Sneak + empty-hand right-click: activate. Repeating activation does not restore HP or deactivate.

Ordinary terrain is not automatically a creature body; assemble your intended body with Sable.

Release is a creative authoring reset, not an ordinary pause: it ends runtime signals/binding and the current life identity while retaining configuration.
manual.sablelife.getting_started.example:
1. Prepare the connected Sable body with its Heart.

2. In creative mode, empty-hand right-click the Heart. Configure modules and Core settings before activation.

3. Close the menu; sneak + empty-hand right-click the Heart to activate.

4. To edit locked settings, use dashboard Release or right-click the body/core with the Creative Release Tool, then reopen the editor.

5. Check settings and markers before activating again.
manual.sablelife.getting_started.trouble:
If editing buttons are gray while alive, Release before changing locked settings. Some live controls remain available.

Release does not fire death loot and does not recover material already removed by completed cleanup.

Holding a block can disguise the Heart instead of opening its empty-hand interface.
manual.sablelife.core.usage:
Configure health, regeneration, protection, death/vanish effects and adaptive defense for the whole creature.

Death XP offers Points (0–30,970) or Levels (0–100). Levels drops a level reward orb: its collector gains the specified levels directly, as with /experience add levels, rather than receiving fixed XP points. Display-unit conversion still uses cumulative XP from level zero; applying a whole-level value changes the amount.

Maximum health scrolls by 5 HP; XP by 1. Percentage regeneration defaults 0%, range 0–100%, scroll ±0.1. Total HP healed per second is fixed regeneration plus maximum health × percentage / 100; max HP 2000 with fixed 10 and 2% heals 50 HP each second. Both obey the same damage-reset quiet delay and never revive dying/dead creatures. Whole-body loot Back returns to Modules.
manual.sablelife.core.settings:
Void death height defaults to the current dimension’s minimum build Y (Overworld −64; Nether/End 0). It tests the living Life Core’s world-space center Y, not storage coordinates or a bedrock block search. Strictly below forces death through armor/adaptive defense.

Set an integer −2048 to 2048 on the protection page; scroll ±1, right-click Apply to restore the dimension default. Dormant bodies and Redstone Cores are unaffected. Survival interaction defaults Off on the protection page. Off blocks survival/adventure right-click operation of life-owned devices, including bearings and frequency changes. Creative authors can operate them. On permits device use while block placement/breaking retain their own rules. Create configuration packets are checked on the server; ordinary block inventories opened before activation or before switching Off are closed and reject item/button clicks when locked. A normal right click on the Life Core still shows its status. Dormant/released structures and independent Redstone Cores retain their usual interaction rules. The setting persists in core saves, configuration copies and respawn templates. Third-party standalone remote-control protocols still need their own compatibility checks.

Death delay is limited to 0–60 s. Names support &0–&f colors, &l bold, &o italic, &n underline, &m strikethrough, &k obfuscated, &r reset, and &#RRGGBB colors. Example: &c&lKilling Machine. Codes count toward the 64-character limit. Module direct kills announce the styled core name; unnamed cores announce block. Projectiles retain their launch name through save/load. Later environmental, fire-tick and status-effect deaths retain vanilla attribution.

Death effects play at death; vanish effects after Death delay. Death/limb cleanup discards directly referenced CBC mounted cannon and Create mechanical-bearing contraption entities when their controller has registered ownership and a death/part job; this includes supported addon payloads, Neo Warfare compact mounts and radar bearings. Ordinary disassembly and unrelated controllers remain unchanged.

Force chunk loading defaults Off; On keeps the active/dying Life Core and connected Sable limbs loaded, following their occupied world chunks. Off, Release, core removal or finished cleanup releases its tickets. Caps: 256 target chunks per creature, 1024 server-wide.

Each stage has one primary sound mix. Restore, left of Preview, resets only that stage’s effect and audio defaults.

Adaptive defense defaults off: threshold 100 HP/s, maximum 80%, window 1 s. Damage is measured after armor and before adaptive reduction.

At sustained 200 DPS the example approaches 50% reduction; 1000 DPS is limited to 80%. Threshold is not a hard DPS cap; maximum is not constant armor; window is not invulnerability.
manual.sablelife.core.example:
1. Open Core settings; configure health and regeneration.

2. On the death and vanish pages, choose patterns, particles and sound mixes separately. Preview both stages; Preview closes the menu so you can view the effect. Reopen the same core to return to the last settings page.

3. Open Defense settings if sustained high DPS protection is desired. Begin with 100 / 80 / 1.

4. Activate and compare isolated hits with sustained attacks.
manual.sablelife.core.troubleshooting:
Adaptive reduction recovers smoothly after recent damage expires. Physical core removal is not an ordinary defended hit. Changing defensive configuration clears its temporary damage statistics.

See Death delay and chunk unloading for leaving the area or closing the world.
manual.sablelife.triggers.usage: Triggers decide when enabled modules activate. Hurt can control either an individual module or a Move set with a fixed combination.
manual.sablelife.triggers.settings:
Always follows active life, or an operational assembled Redstone Core. Mark redstone reads a marked input. Internal wireless uses body-local channels; external wireless uses red/blue frequency items.

Move set actions are scheduled by their controller. Hurt has separate response, signal duration and cooldown settings.

Attack Interval and sound Start are separate clocks.
manual.sablelife.triggers.example:
1. Select Trigger when hurt on an independent attack.

2. Open its hurt settings and choose response, duration and cooldown.

3. For a combination, instead set action modules to move set and the controlling Move set to Hurt.

4. Independent Hurt modules may run alongside that combination.
manual.sablelife.triggers.troubleshootin:
A very short signal can allow only one shot or hit. Hurt cooldown throttles new responses, not individual attack hits.

Do not treat an internal channel number as an external item frequency. Wireless channels can have names up to 40 characters: use the name field and Enter or the check button. Sidebar rows keep number and state before the name. Names persist and do not restart signals; blank clears a name. The Wireless page fills the available height; its density control shares the Modules setting. Smaller density shows more channel rows while keeping the selected channel when paging changes.
manual.sablelife.sound_timeline.usage: The shared sound editor supports multiple layers for modules, death, vanish and BGM.
manual.sablelife.sound_timeline.settings:
Each layer has Start, Pitch, Volume, Range, Limit and Fade. Limit 0 allows natural effects playback or native BGM looping. Fade occupies the final seconds within the limit, and playback stops at the limit. Fade 0 cuts off immediately. For example, Limit 1.5 and Fade 0.5 starts fading at 1 second and stops at 1.5 seconds. Fade longer than the limit uses the entire playback interval. Fading cannot extend a sound that ends naturally sooner.

Dashed natural tails are not measured file durations.

Mouse wheel over Start, Pitch, Volume, Limit and Fade adjusts by 0.1; Range adjusts by 8. Fade accepts 0–600 seconds.
manual.sablelife.sound_timeline.example:
1. Open a sound button; search the left library. MC and OGG tools are inside this page.

2. Double-left-click a library or selected sound to listen. Right-click a library sound to add it, then add another layer.

3. Set starts to 0 and 0.4 s; adjust each pitch/volume.

4. Preview one layer or the mix, stop and return.
manual.sablelife.sound_timeline.troubles:
Closing preview stops its queue. Effect tails may finish after an attack phase, but disabling/deleting their source cancels them.

Custom OGG resources must be present on listening clients. Hearing range is not attack range.
manual.sablelife.retaliation.usage: Example: a fixed hurt-triggered combo plus an independent extra reaction.
manual.sablelife.retaliation.settings: Hurt settings belong to the controlling Move set; scheduled actions use move set triggers. An independent extra action uses its own Hurt cooldown.
manual.sablelife.retaliation.example:
1. Add and mark an attack and Trigger sound.

2. Set both to move set triggers and add them to one Move.

3. Set the Move set to Hurt and choose a one-response mode and cooldown suitable for the sequence.

4. Optionally add a separate marked Hurt attack.

5. Damage once, then rapidly again; verify both response cooldowns.
manual.sablelife.retaliation.troubleshoo: A missing required action invalidates the whole reaction. Hurt Once ends the cancelled reaction instead of endlessly retrying it; a new hurt event is required.
manual.sablelife.survival_core.usage: A survival-craftable control core with a purple signal crystal and camouflage casing. It runs harmless redstone programs without activating life.
manual.sablelife.survival_core.settings:
Supports Move set, Pulse sequence, Wireless redstone, Target sensor, Target alignment, Auto facing, Item display, Sound, Trigger sound, BGM and the Wireless page internal cycles/external RX/TX.

Master controls output. Assemble the body first; exactly one core is allowed across all connected parts, including life cores.

No attacks, commands or Hurt. Move set schedules only allowed control modules; HP conditions do not apply.

Sound names and editors are shared: Hurt sound is disabled, and BGM runs on its trigger for nearby listeners instead of waiting for combat. Inactive combat settings remain stored for reuse with a Life Core.
manual.sablelife.survival_core.example:
1. Craft one core: redstone block / redstone torch / redstone block; repeater / amethyst shard / comparator; redstone block / lever / redstone block.

2. Place it in a body and assemble using the normal Sable assembly workflow.

3. Empty-hand right-click to configure. Add Wireless redstone, mark an outlet or choose Frequency Item.

4. Choose Always for continuous output, or connect an internal/external channel trigger. Use Master to pause. No life activation is needed.
manual.sablelife.survival_core.troublesh:
Not assembled, duplicate core or Master Off stops output. Newly placed duplicates are rejected; duplicates introduced by assembly, merge or reload suspend output until removed.

Match frequency items and choose the correct trigger/channel. Copy and reload retain only the harmless whitelist.
manual.sablelife.move_set.settings:
Conditions filter distance, HP band and line of sight before Weighted / Priority selection. Forward reference defines facing. Cooldown limits reuse; Rest spaces moves.

Rules and timing are owned entirely by Move set; no Move dispatcher is required. Existing saved Move set rules load automatically.

Each Move set selects moves, tracks cooldowns and runs its timeline independently. When two controllers reference the same module, their active action windows are combined as an OR signal. The module keeps one runtime and its own interval; it is not duplicated, queued or restarted by the second overlapping controller. It remains triggered until all referencing action windows end.
manual.sablelife.move_set.example: Create two marked attacks with move set triggers. Open Edit move set, add a Move and two actions; start the second at 0.5 s, then configure Conditions / rhythm.
manual.sablelife.move_set.troubleshootin:
ANY required referenced action missing, disabled, disconnected or unmarked makes the whole Move ineligible.

Running damage cancels remaining dispatch; other complete Moves continue. If all Moves fail, the controller waits. It never just skips the broken action.

Wireless redstone and commands retain no-Mark exceptions.

Shared modules and channels are not reserved or isolated between controllers. For example, action windows 0–3 s and 2–5 s keep one shared module triggered continuously from 0–5 s. Use separate module instances and channels when independent behavior is needed. Overlapping sequence channel outputs combine by maximum power. Avoid conflicting assignments yourself; no automatic arbitration is applied.
manual.sablelife.wireless_redstone.setti:
Power controls strength; Hold follows activation, Pulse uses pulse duration. Faces selects all or marked face. Red/blue items define external frequency; ignore them for Mark-only output.

Reverse signal defaults Off. On swaps zero and configured power for both destinations. Hold outputs while idle and stops while triggered. Pulse normally outputs, interrupts for the configured pulse duration on a rising trigger, then restores output even if the trigger remains high. Disabled/invalid modules, dormant/dead cores and master Off always output zero. Outputs to this core's Wireless channel; 0 disables it. Enable the channel and select Sequence / internal. Uses strength, Hold/Pulse and inversion. No Mark or frequency items required; all three destinations can work together. Highest strength wins across producers. Use different input/output channels to avoid self-latching.
manual.sablelife.wireless_redstone.examp: Move Set directly schedules Wireless Redstone with Trigger=Move set and internal output channel 10. Enable Wireless channel 10 as Sequence / internal. Armor stays Always; rule 2 reads internal channel 10 while powered. No Pulse Sequence bridge needed. Mark and external red/blue outputs can run alongside it.
manual.sablelife.wireless_redstone.troub: Unbound, missing, disabled or non-Sequence channels do not receive internal output. Default 0 preserves old configurations. Deleting a channel unbinds matching outputs and shifts later indices; portable presets unbind internal output. No destinations means no emitted signal. Other high producers on the same channel can mask an inverted low.
manual.sablelife.command.settings: Impulse / Repeat / Chain determine behavior. Conditional requires the immediately preceding row to succeed in this pass. Repeat interval throttles repeat rows.
manual.sablelife.command.example: Open Edit commands, add a blank row, type say hi, use Tab and Save command. Choose Impulse, enable and trigger. Add a conditional Chain row to test dependencies.
manual.sablelife.command.troubleshooting: Save does not execute. Check permissions/server command settings. Executes at the moving core without Mark.
manual.sablelife.melee.settings:
Two marks define a volume. Start distance shifts it; horizontal/vertical angles rotate it and its offset direction around the center.

Hit limit is per target per continuous activation. 0 = unlimited, still subject to Interval. Burn time accepts 0–30 seconds, default 0. Successful damage ignites the target; a blocked hit does not.
manual.sablelife.melee.example: Mark two corners on the same body, set hit limit 3 and Interval, adjust offsets and Preview. Hold activation while a target enters/leaves.
manual.sablelife.melee.troubleshooting: Leaving does not reset hit count; ending activation does. Hurt Once can be too short for repeated hits.
manual.sablelife.flame.settings:
Speed controls outward travel, Width spread and Range reach. Start distance clears the muzzle.

Particle opens the shared selector: normal/soul fire or mixed supported particle types, each with size and lifetime. Lifetime 0 covers the journey.

Effect adds status effects on successful damage hits; Damage and Burn remain separate.
manual.sablelife.flame.example:
Mark the outlet, choose particles and size in Particle, then add Slowness with duration/level in Effect.

Set Burn to 0 for no ignition, Preview, then trigger against a test target. Adjust Width moderately.
manual.sablelife.flame.troubleshooting:
Particle size is not the damage hitbox. Short particle lifetime can cut the visual off early; 0 follows range/speed.

Effects follow successful hits and the same interval.

Existing blue-fire/size settings migrate automatically. Check direction and interval if intermittent.
manual.sablelife.particles.settings:
Area uses two marks; Point/Line/Ring/Sphere use a separate single mark. Start distance offsets origin. Radius/length shapes it.

Ring height 0 preserves one circle; positive height extends a hollow cylinder from the origin along the selected direction. Density is shared over its surface, without multiplying emission per layer. Outward/inward propagation expands or contracts radially at each axial section.

Random/Even and sphere Inside/Surface select distribution. Density is per particle type; size/lifetime are in the particle editor.

Line/Ring/Sphere Propagation can travel outward from center or inward from the endpoint/edge. Speed is blocks per tick; lifetime 0 covers the path.

Motion trail fills body movement/rotation gaps; Only while moving controls emission timing.
manual.sablelife.particles.example:
Choose Sphere, mark one point, set radius, Random and Inside, then Preview.

Switch to Area and mark two corners; switching back retains the point mark. Line supports placed or spray modes.

For a tube, choose Ring, radius 2, Ring height 8, direction Up and density 32. Preview the three circular sections and side edges. Increase density for a less sparse wall.
manual.sablelife.particles.troubleshooti:
Clear affects only the current mark mode. High density/many types cost more particles.

Native friction/gravity do not shorten controlled travel. A custom lifetime shorter than the journey still cuts it off.
manual.sablelife.linear_movement.setting:
Fixed distance is the legacy default: distance and horizontal/vertical angles steer movement.

Toward target selects the nearest eligible target within Target search range. The marked movement point stops N blocks before the target center; N is Stop before target. This is center distance, not a guarantee of collision-box clearance. At or within N, no movement is needed; no target means waiting. The target position is sampled when charging starts and is not updated to chase later movement. Horizontal mode fixes the endpoint X/Z while preserving current movement height; 3D mode fixes the complete endpoint. Creative players can be included. Use target height defaults Off: keep current movement-point height and use a horizontal stopping gap. On uses the recorded target height and a full 3D stopping distance.

Target mode replaces fixed distance/direction/angle settings without rotating the construct. Teleport and Travel keep their existing collision/loaded-area checks. Charge, departure and arrival have separate effects/sounds.

Teleport checks destination; Travel checks terrain by default. Force movement defaults Off. On skips terrain/body collision prechecks, while retaining loaded-destination/world-bound checks. Forced Travel follows planned translation despite physics pushback. Normal physics still applies after completion.
manual.sablelife.linear_movement.example:
Mark a starting face, choose Teleport with short distance and zero angles, Preview on flat ground. Switch to Travel and configure speed for gradual movement.

For target movement, select Toward target, choose target type and search range, then set Stop before target to 2. A target 10 blocks from the mark gives an 8-block displacement. Preview before triggering; the same target mode works with Teleport and Travel.

Facing example: if the marked face points North and the selected player is South behind the machine, target movement displaces it South while retaining its North-facing orientation. To face the player first, configure Auto facing with a matching target type/range, allow enough time to align, then start Linear movement. In Move set, place turning before displacement.
manual.sablelife.linear_movement.trouble:
Small contact tolerance permits touching ground, not embedding in walls. Large bodies need clearance for all parts. Movement checks each connected rigid body’s contact-adjusted enclosing box against terrain collision shapes and other Sable bodies’ enclosing boxes. Empty corners in rotated/sparse bodies can therefore block before a real body voxel touches. Travel approaches the closest allowed position then stops; Teleport cancels if its required path or destination check fails. Ordinary living-entity hitboxes are not included in this precheck. Target stop distance does not override collision.

Target stopping distance measures the marked point to target center, not two collision-box surfaces. Once movement completes, ordinary physics resumes; this module does not hold the construct in the air or lock its position.
manual.sablelife.arena.usage: Manage the creature leaving a fixed arena, with nearby-player warnings and optional punishment or return.
manual.sablelife.arena.settings:
Radius uses a fixed horizontal center. Countdown starts when the creature leaves, not players.

Nearby-player death defaults on; force return/full health defaults off and takes precedence when on.

No-nearby-player return is separate.
manual.sablelife.arena.example: Mark center and set radius. Disable nearby-player death while testing; choose force return if wanted. Move the creature out and observe.
manual.sablelife.arena.troubleshooting: Center stays fixed in world; return preserves height. Check nearby survival-player range for punishment.
manual.sablelife.homing.settings:
Formation and fan rotations use the marked face. Offset/height position hovering shells; deploy and charge precede launch.

Target filters, tracking and lifetime control pursuit.
manual.sablelife.homing.example: Choose Arc (n), both rotations 0; view from the marked face front. Set targets and Preview before triggering.
manual.sablelife.homing.troubleshooting: Above-view appearance differs. Verify marked face before changing rotation; check target filters.
manual.sablelife.mortar.settings: Aim, target, speed and launch angle define the arc. Warning color applies from its first frame. Explosion/block damage are separate.
manual.sablelife.mortar.example: Mark launch face, choose target mode and a non-red warning color, then trigger in open terrain.
manual.sablelife.mortar.troubleshooting: Check arc clearance/target range for misses. A large hitbox may need more Start distance.
manual.sablelife.navigation.usage: Output navigation signals for a player-designed movement and aiming mechanism.
manual.sablelife.navigation.settings:
Target range, forward reference, tracking, dead zones and lock govern navigation signals.

Reverse redstone directions swaps left/right, up/down and front/back while preserving strength.

The player designs the physical movement/aiming mechanism.
manual.sablelife.navigation.example: Mark reference, choose targets and configure output connections; wire them to your own turning mechanism and test both axes.
manual.sablelife.navigation.troubleshoot: This outputs signals; use Linear movement for direct travel. Verify wiring and mechanical design.
manual.sablelife.health_phase.settings: Edit phases from the dashboard. Up to 64 independent rows with enabled state, exclusive lower/inclusive upper HP, output channel, strength, Hold/Enter and pulse duration. The outer Trigger gates all rows. Overlaps can output multiple channels together; highest strength wins on a shared channel. Outputs require enabled, configured Sequence internal/external TX channels; 0 is unbound.
manual.sablelife.health_phase.example: One module: 70–100% -> channel 1, 40–70% -> channel 2, 0–40% -> channel 3, all Hold. Exactly 70% belongs to row 2; exactly 40% to row 3. Each Enter row has its own clock: hits do not restart it. Leaving its band or losing the outer trigger cancels it; reentry fires again.
manual.sablelife.health_phase.troublesho: Old single settings become the first row. Ordinary saves preserve rows; presets keep bands/modes but unbind outputs. Deleting a channel unbinds matching rows and shifts later indices. Lower must be below upper. Disabling or editing other rows does not restart this row's pulse. The editor shows the selected row's output status.
manual.sablelife.sequence.settings: Step outputs/times are edited in the sequence editor. Once/Repeat controls replay; Stop on low and reset source/channel govern restart.
manual.sablelife.sequence.example: Add two steps with different channels and timings, connect matching receivers, test Once then Repeat.
manual.sablelife.sequence.troubleshootin: Reset source must match as well as reset channel.
manual.sablelife.sound.settings: Approach, hurt and ambient events each use sound mixes. Event ranges, cooldowns and ambient timing decide when they start. Block contact sound is configured in Trigger sound.
manual.sablelife.sound.example: Open an event sound, add layers, Preview, then configure event timing/range and test that event.
manual.sablelife.sound.troubleshooting: Hearing range and event detection differ; empty mixes are silent. See Sound combinations.
manual.sablelife.trigger_sound.settings:
Trigger-driven sound mix, with playback mode, cooldown and repeat interval. Each layer owns Start/Pitch/Volume/Range.

Block contact sound has its own On/Off switch, mix, six local directions, distance and cooldown. While the module trigger is active, entering contact plays once; continued contact does not loop. Its cooldown is independent of the ordinary trigger sound. Both mixes can be used together; clear the ordinary trigger mix when only contact audio is wanted. Contact markers and preview follow the selected local face as the body turns.
manual.sablelife.trigger_sound.example: Mark its origin, add a sound mix and choose move set or Hurt trigger. Test in a Move or independently.
manual.sablelife.trigger_sound.troublesh: Action duration does not automatically truncate a sound. Use layer limit for cutoff.
manual.sablelife.bgm.settings: Start behavior, radius and fade govern background music. Layers retain delays/limits; natural playback follows BGM looping.
manual.sablelife.bgm.example: Add music layers, Preview, configure radius/fade, activate and approach/leave the creature.
manual.sablelife.bgm.troubleshooting: No Mark is needed. Nearby creatures compete for the music source; custom resources must exist locally.
manual.sablelife.loot.settings: Whole-body and part loot share the new editor: 27 samples and inventory on the left, quantity, chance/weight, mode and draws on the right. Empty-handed left-click only selects. Inputs/buttons/wheel edit values. Chance steps ±5, weight ±1 and quantity ±1. Chance independently checks every slot; weighted mode draws from positive weights. Quantity separately controls each dropped stack. Existing limits remain: whole-body weights 0–100, part weights 0–1000.
manual.sablelife.loot.example: With an item, left copies its stack and right adds one. Empty-handed right removes one; Clear deletes the sample. Shift-left/right raises/lowers the rule. Shift-click inventory copies into the first empty sample without consuming items. Ordinary inventory operations remain available. Custom names/components are preserved.
manual.sablelife.loot.troubleshooting: Loot authoring is read-only while the creature is active; select samples to inspect them. Samples are not storage and cannot be extracted, collected or thrown. Chance mode ignores draws. Existing samples, chance/weight values and draw counts are preserved. Part drops remain separate from whole-body drops.
manual.sablelife.armor.settings: Mark selects the whole affected part; the outer Trigger gates the module. Edit phase rules to add enabled rows with internal channel/external RX, input channel and damage modifier (-100% to +1000%, wheel ±5). Channel 0 is unbound. Rows apply according to their powered/unpowered condition. Lowest matching modifier across rows/modules wins without stacking; no match means normal damage. Global adaptive defense follows these modifiers. Each row can apply while powered or unpowered; unpowered mode pauses when signaled and resumes when the signal ends.
manual.sablelife.armor.example: Use Trigger Always: channel 1 = -100%, channel 2 = -50%, channel 3 = +50%. Health Phase holds the stage channels for immunity, reduced damage and vulnerability. If channels 1 and 3 overlap, -100% wins. For default immunity that pauses on channel 4, add a -100% rule on input 4 with Apply while unpowered. Immunity resumes when that signal ends.
manual.sablelife.armor.troubleshooting: Previous single values are not migrated: add rules again. Disabled, unbound, missing-channel or invalid-Mark rows do not apply. Each row decides whether powered or unpowered input applies. Deleting a channel unbinds its rules. Portable presets retain modifiers and conditions but unbind inputs. Ordinary saves and structure copies preserve rules.
manual.sablelife.sensor.settings: Detection radius is 1–64 blocks, default 12. Shape/radius/inner radius/front width/direction define detection; target and line of sight filter entities. Mark receives 15 weak redstone power through the selected face, so a marked lamp lights up. It no longer emits from all faces. Internal output channel 0 means unbound; select an enabled Module output channel to route it. Red/blue frequency items provide additional external output. Channel signal strength does not change Mark strength. Invert signal powers outputs while no target is detected and clears them when a target is detected; disabled, inactive or untriggered sensors stay off.
manual.sablelife.sensor.example: Mark sensor face, choose shape/targets/range, Preview and connect its signal outputs to receivers.
manual.sablelife.sensor.troubleshooting: Out-of-shape and sight-blocked targets are ignored. Check routing independently.
manual.sablelife.laser.settings:
Charge precedes beam fire. Length/width define collision; beam hits/hit interval differ from firing Interval.

Tracking and sweep change aim.

Break blocks defaults Off. Clear whole line removes breakable blocks intersecting the beam centerline during firing. Cut forward begins at the first obstruction and advances toward maximum beam length at Breaking speed (blocks/s, default 16). Destruction proceeds every firing tick, separately from entity hit intervals.

Own connected body is skipped. Unbreakable blocks, protected lifeform blocks and unloaded chunks stop the cut. No block item drops are created by the laser; containers can have their own removal effects. Breaking speed does not extend the burst: set enough Beam hits × Hit interval time to reach the endpoint. Signal loss or burst completion stops cutting. Charging and Preview never destroy blocks.
manual.sablelife.laser.example: Mark origin, choose aiming, short charge and safe length, Preview and trigger. Edit charge/fire sounds separately.
manual.sablelife.laser.troubleshooting:
Short activation may end before charging completes. Beam width is not particle size.

Automatic targeting still needs an initially visible target; use Fixed direction to start cutting a wall directly. A tracked target moving behind a breakable wall can be followed during firing. Extremely many cuts share a 1024-block removal budget per world tick; remaining obstructions stay until a later firing tick.
manual.sablelife.ground_strike.settings: Mode/radius/range/rays or random count control placement. Start distance, wave delay and step control progression; warning precedes damage.
manual.sablelife.ground_strike.example: Mark origin, choose mode/color, Preview a short range then test; expand rays/area after confirming.
manual.sablelife.ground_strike.troublesh: Check placement/target modes; warning time is not repetition interval.
manual.sablelife.quake.settings: Line/ring/area and marked/target-foot origin shape the wave. Range/width/speed and wave gap control propagation. Grounded rules filter targets.
manual.sablelife.quake.example: Mark origin, choose line/ring, modest range and warning; Preview then test a grounded target.
manual.sablelife.quake.troubleshooting: Airborne targets may be excluded. Wave travel is separate from attack interval.
manual.sablelife.pull.settings:
Release position can use a marked point or the nearest eligible target as a fixed cast center; target mode needs no Mark. Radius chooses victims around that center.

Stopping distance brakes/stops attraction near the center, not detection range.

Defaults: beacon activate warning, beacon ambient pull. Strength/speed/stop distance control motion. Warning and pull duration separate anticipation and action.
manual.sablelife.pull.example: Mark center, choose targets/modest strength, Preview and test stop distance.
manual.sablelife.pull.troubleshooting: Check range/line of sight. Entity types may react differently to motion.
manual.sablelife.pulse.usage: Apply radial damage and knockback pulses around a marked origin.
manual.sablelife.pulse.settings: Radius, damage and knockback define a radial pulse. Start distance offsets origin; Interval repeats it. Fixed boundary ring preserves the original style. Outward sphere expands from the release center to Radius over 0.05–10 seconds, default 0.5 seconds. Cosmetic only: damage and knockback still resolve immediately, with no extra hits during expansion. Center and wave/boundary particles can be selected separately, with size and lifetime. Empty a group to disable it. Outward particle lifetime is at least the expansion time so it reaches the boundary.
manual.sablelife.pulse.example: Mark origin, small radius/knockback, Preview then test one nearby target.
manual.sablelife.pulse.troubleshooting: Check target and interval. Knockback cannot guarantee motion through obstacles.
manual.sablelife.arrow.settings:
Projectile, speed, scatter count, start distance and residual time keep their existing behavior.

Explosion and block breaking remain separate. Landing sound opens an independent Sound Mix for block impacts. The untouched default keeps the native arrow sound; a custom mix replaces it, and an empty mix is silent. Entity-hit sounds are unchanged. Landing settings are frozen per shot and persist through reload. Accepted explosive block impacts also play a configured landing mix.
manual.sablelife.arrow.example: Mark the firing face and set Landing sound layers separately from Fire sound. Preview the mix and test arrows against a nearby wall. Start distance and flight speed are already available.
manual.sablelife.arrow.troubleshooting: Clearing Landing sound does not mute Fire sound or explosions. Epic Fight ordinary Guard excludes projectile damage; native Parrying allows projectiles with an eligible weapon.
manual.sablelife.gun.settings:
Speed/count/interval define volleys. Visual size differs from hitbox. Start distance moves large projectiles clear of the muzzle.

Explosion and block breaking are separate.
manual.sablelife.gun.example: Mark firing face, choose one projectile and safe reach, Preview direction and trigger. Increase count or add effects after basic firing works.
manual.sablelife.gun.troubleshooting: Immediate collision usually needs clearance or Start distance; check direction before increasing damage.
manual.sablelife.basic_operations.usage:
Start here before configuring individual modules.

1. Getting Started: core inspection, activation and Release.

2. Module management: add, rename, save, disable and delete.

3. Mark system: point, area, direction, replace, cancel and clear.

4. Preview: inspect geometry and troubleshoot unavailable buttons.

5. Triggers and signals: choose activation and connect channels.

6. Sound combinations: select and test layered audio.
manual.sablelife.basic_operations.settin: These chapters are in Guides at the start of the directory. Search their localized or English title, or IDs getting_started, simple_start, module_management, marking_system and preview_system. Opening a manual chapter is read only.
manual.sablelife.basic_operations.exampl:
1. Read Getting Started to enter the core editor, then A Simple Start for the module workflow.

2. Add one module and save its basic settings.

3. Read Mark system, select a valid origin and Preview.

4. Choose its trigger.

5. Activate the creature for a real test; return to the relevant troubleshooting tab if it fails.
manual.sablelife.basic_operations.troubl: Separate these states: module enabled, marker valid, trigger active, and creature alive. A valid marker alone does not start an attack; Preview is not activation.
manual.sablelife.module_management.usage: Manage virtual modules inside the Heart rather than placing a separate physical block for every ability. Each entry retains its type even after renaming.
manual.sablelife.module_management.setti:
+ Add module opens a separate catalog with All, Signals, Attacks, Functions and Presets. Select an entry and click Load modules, or double-click to add it.

Search by localized or English name and ID. Rows fill downward before continuing in the next column; bottom arrows change pages.

Use the arrows beside Add module to reorder existing modules, or the preset arrows to reorder personal favorites.

Preset Delete requires two clicks and is disabled for built-in modules.

Enter a name or number and press its checkmark to apply; choice buttons send their changes when selected.

Enable/Disable controls an existing module without deleting its settings. Delete uses a second confirmation click.

Language, left of Density, switches Minecraft between English and Simplified Chinese without restarting, with a brief resource reload. The language selection is saved.

Density adjusts text and spacing; arrows page the module and property lists.

Mouse wheel applies numeric edits immediately: counts/power/whole-block detection ranges use 1, angles use 5, and small sizes/motion retain decimal precision.
manual.sablelife.module_management.examp:
1. Click + Add module, select a type and click Load modules, or double-click it.

2. Select the new list entry. Enter a useful name and click its checkmark.

3. Set numeric fields with their checkmarks and select mode buttons.

4. Hover a renamed entry to confirm its original type; use ? for help.

5. Disable to keep it for later, or click Delete and confirm if removing it.
manual.sablelife.module_management.troub:
Red input text indicates invalid values; use the displayed limits.

A renamed module is still the same referenced module. Disabling/deleting a required Move set action can make its whole Move unavailable.

Module enabled does not mean the creature is activated or its trigger is satisfied.
manual.sablelife.marking_system.usage:
Mark connects a virtual ability to a body point, face or area. Ordinary marks follow the marked body position and rotation.

Arena is an exception: its marked center stays fixed in world space. Marking changes configuration, not the physical blocks.
manual.sablelife.marking_system.settings:
Point: choose one connected body surface; the face supplies the marked direction.

Area: Melee and Particle Area use two block corners on the SAME rigid body, up to 32 blocks per axis including corners. Connected articulated limbs are not necessarily the same rigid body.

Particle Area and point patterns store marks separately.

Navigation asks for a horizontal face toward the construct front. Arena allows a terrain/body point as a fixed center.

Core modules do not need Mark; Wireless redstone may use external output without one.
manual.sablelife.marking_system.example:
1. Select the module, then click Mark area/origin; the menu closes and a selection hint appears.

2. For a point, right-click the intended body face. For an area, right-click the first and second corners on one rigid body. Successful selection returns to the dashboard.

3. Check marker status, then Preview the direction/volume.

4. To replace a mark, click Mark area/origin again and finish the new selection.

5. To cancel: Esc, or sneak-right-click a BLOCK. The previously saved mark remains.

6. To CLEAR: enter marking again, aim into AIR and sneak-right-click. Saved marks for the current mode are cleared and the dashboard reopens.
manual.sablelife.marking_system.troubles:
Clearing only works during an active mark-selection session and when the server ray hits no block within reach. Looking at a block while sneaking cancels instead.

A wrong body or oversized second corner is rejected; finish a valid selection or cancel. Selection expires after two minutes, or if permissions/configuration change.

Destroyed/disconnected marked parts invalidate required modules; clearing a required mark returns to Not marked with Preview disabled.

For particles, clearing Area does not erase the separately stored point mark.
manual.sablelife.preview_system.usage: Preview inspects configured origin, direction, volume or path before a real activation. Geometry previews do not execute the attack or move the creature. Particle previews can display decorative particles.
manual.sablelife.preview_system.settings:
Ordinary marker previews last about five seconds and are sent only to the requesting player. A valid marker is not a trigger.

Not marked, missing/disconnected body parts and unavailable permissions can disable Preview.

Some core/no-Mark modules have dedicated editors or no marker preview. Wireless redstone can output externally without Mark even though a marked-output preview is unavailable.
manual.sablelife.preview_system.example:
1. Apply settings and complete the required mark.

2. Click Preview; inspect the front face, area or movement path in the world.

3. Reopen the dashboard and adjust direction, Start distance, angles or range if needed.

4. Repeat Preview, then separately activate the creature and satisfy its trigger for a real test.

5. For sounds or Core death/vanish effects, use their own Preview controls.
manual.sablelife.preview_system.troubles:
A gray Preview does not by itself mean a no-Mark module cannot run. Check whether that module requires Mark.

Linear movement red path/destination means collision, not a trigger error.

For area marks, compare the whole rotated volume rather than only its center.

Effect previews are visual/audio demonstrations; death-effect preview is not actual creature death.
dashboard.sablelife.particle_trail_help: Interpolates particle emission along the moving/rotating body path. Off emits only at its current position. Different from Only while moving; stationary bodies look the same.
dashboard.sablelife.particle_motion_only: Only emits when the marked body moves or rotates. This controls when to emit; Motion trail controls whether to fill gaps.
dashboard.sablelife.particle_propagation: Line/Ring/Sphere: Pattern default keeps placement (Line spray still moves outward). From center travels to Length/Radius; reverse travels from the endpoint/edge to center. Speed is blocks per tick. Native friction/gravity do not shorten the path. Lifetime 0 covers the journey; a shorter custom lifetime cuts it off. Drift and sphere interior fill apply to static placement.
dashboard.sablelife.description_auto_fac: Directly turns the connected creature toward its selected target while active. The marked face defines its front.
dashboard.sablelife.auto_facing_help: Mark the front face. Default: nearest selected target within 64 blocks, 180 deg/s, horizontal turning. Vertical tracking also tilts the entire creature. Terrain/other machines block turning; large bodies may turn more slowly. Direct movement takes precedence; only the first active facing controller operates. If vertical rotation is blocked, safe horizontal turning continues.
dashboard.sablelife.facing_state_front_i: Mark a side face, or enable vertical tracking
dashboard.sablelife.facing_state_blocked: Rotation blocked by terrain / body unavailable
manual.sablelife.auto_facing.settings:
Target type uses the shared player/mob/all/lifeform categories. Range limits selection; Turn speed is degrees per second, default 180.

Horizontal tracking is default; vertical tracking tilts the whole machine. Creative players may be included.

Line of sight defaults Off; On selects the nearest visible target, ignoring your own connected body.
manual.sablelife.auto_facing.example: Add Auto facing, mark its front face, select Target type, range and speed. Preview the front line, then activate with Always trigger. Move an eligible target around it.
manual.sablelife.auto_facing.troubleshoo:
No visible eligible target means no rotation when Line of sight is On. Horizontal mode needs a nonvertical front face; enable vertical tracking for other faces.

Collision check defaults On: terrain/bounding boxes block unsafe rotation; blocked vertical rotation still allows clear horizontal turning.

Off skips that check and forces rotation even while intersecting terrain, at the configured turn speed.

Direct movement wins; first active facing module controls the machine. Navigation still outputs signals for your mechanical design.

Linear movement takes control from charging until movement finishes, including the teleport tick, so Auto facing pauses during that interval. Target-directed displacement does not itself rotate the machine. Turn before moving if the front must face the target; turning may remain incomplete if blocked or given too little time.
dashboard.sablelife.mark_auto_facing_poi: Right-click the front face. Horizontal tracking needs a side face; enable vertical tracking for top/bottom fronts. Esc cancels; sneak-right-click air clears.
sound_timeline.sablelife.row_help: Left-click selects; double-click listens using this layer’s settings, without its start delay.
core.sablelife.restore_help: Restore this stage’s default particles, pattern, count/spread and primary sound mix. Death instant: fireworks and blast sound. After delay: disappearance smoke, no sound. Does not change health, Death delay or the other stage.
dashboard.sablelife.navigation_invert_he: Swap left/right, up/down and front/back output faces while preserving strength. Example: left 8 becomes right 8. No target remains silent; disabling the module or ending its trigger shuts outputs off.
dashboard.sablelife.facing_state_vertica: Vertical rotation blocked; horizontal tracking continues
core.sablelife.xp_units_help: Points: 0–30,970 raw XP, dropped as ordinary XP orbs. Levels: 0–100; the player collecting the level reward orb gains that many levels directly, like /experience add <player> <amount> levels. Switching display units uses cumulative XP from level zero; applying a value changes the amount. Existing pending death jobs retain their saved reward mode.
manual.sablelife.simple_start.usage:
Purple modules handle signals, red modules attacks, yellow modules functions.

Search localized or English names and stable IDs. Reading this manual does not execute abilities or change settings.
manual.sablelife.simple_start.settings:
Modules must be enabled and their triggers satisfied. Required markers must remain connected. Core modules and Wireless redstone have no-Mark exceptions.

Life Core uses life activation. Redstone Core supports its control/sound whitelist on an assembled unique-core body without life activation.
manual.sablelife.simple_start.example:
1. Open Virtual modules and + Add module.

2. Choose a module and adjust its settings.

3. Click Mark area/origin where required and select its body face or two corners.

4. Preview, choose a trigger, then activate the creature.

5. Open ? for module-specific help.
manual.sablelife.simple_start.troublesho:
During marking, Shift + right-click in air clears the current mark. Esc or a sneak-click on a block cancels without clearing. A cleared required marker disables Preview.

Renaming preserves module type; hover the list entry to identify it.
control.sablelife.unassembled: Assemble this body to enable control
control.sablelife.duplicate: Only one core per connected body; remove the extra core
control.sablelife.ready: Redstone control ready; no life activation needed
control.sablelife.paused: Redstone control paused by master switch
tooltip.sablelife.redstone_core: Harmless redstone control. Assemble one core per body; no life activation needed.
dashboard.sablelife.control_audio_help: Redstone Core has no combat or hurt events. BGM plays while triggered for nearby listeners; combat-start settings are inactive. Shared settings are retained for copying to a Life Core.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_target: Checks this target type at selection time; does not control aiming or movement.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchFar: At least one target must be within this distance.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchCool: Starts when chosen; prevents selecting this move again until it ends.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchWeig: Weight 20 is twice as likely as weight 10 among eligible moves.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchBusy: Waits at least this long, and longer if its sequence is still running.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchRest: After the move and its sequence finish, wait before choosing another move.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_phaseUpper: This construct’s current HP percentage must be at or below this value. Together with minimum HP, controls when the move is eligible; for example maximum 50 and minimum 0 enables it at half health or below.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_phaseLower: This construct’s own HP percentage must be above this value; 0 is the lowest boundary. Use it to assign moves to health phases. This is not the target’s HP.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchNear: Target must not be closer than this distance.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchCone: 360 accepts all directions; smaller angles require a target in front.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchFron: Defines forward relative to the core and rotates with it. Used only when target angle is below 360° to decide whether a target lies in the allowed cone. It does not change projectile direction.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_lineOfSight: Targets hidden behind walls do not make this move eligible.
moveset.sablelife.rule_help_dispatchRepe: Avoid repeat chooses another eligible move if possible; allows this move when it is the only eligible one.
manual.sablelife.death_unloading.usage: Death delay is tracked by a world-owned death job, independently of the core block ticking. Leaving the area does not revive a dying creature or restart its delay.
manual.sablelife.death_unloading.setting:
While the server continues ticking, death countdowns continue even if the creature chunks are unloaded or a multiplayer player logs out.

With Force chunk loading Off, unloaded blocks are not force-loaded: removal and loot/XP settlement wait until their required chunks are loaded. With On, the active/dying connected body stays loaded and necessary death reward chunks are held until settlement, within loading limits.

Exiting a single-player world, shutting down the server or pausing its ticks saves/freezes the remaining delay; real offline time is not deducted.
manual.sablelife.death_unloading.example:
Set Death delay to 60 s. After death, stay for 20 s, then teleport away for 45 s while the server continues ticking. On return the delay has expired; pending loaded-body cleanup/settlement proceeds instead of restarting a 40 s timer.

If you closed the single-player world after the first 20 s, reopening resumes about 40 s, regardless of real time away.
manual.sablelife.death_unloading.trouble:
Void-height death uses the same death effects, delay, cleanup and loot/XP locations; it does not rescue or move rewards to safe ground. Height detection requires the living core to tick.

An unloaded corpse may remain saved until it can be cleaned safely; this is pending cleanup, not renewed life. Large bodies can take several ticks to clean.

Loading applies to world-space body coverage, not only the core block or Sable storage coordinates. The settings page reports target chunk count or an exceeded limit.

Loot/XP settlement is recorded to avoid duplicate rewards. Chunk loading cannot make a stopped or paused server continue ticking.
core.sablelife.force_chunk_help: On: keeps an active or dying Life Core and its connected body loaded, following movement. Off, Release, core removal or completed cleanup releases only its own loading tickets. Default Off. Max 256 target chunks per creature, 1024 server-wide. This cannot run a stopped/paused server.
core.sablelife.void_death_help: An ALIVE Life Core below this world-space Y dies regardless of armor/adaptive defense. Default: current dimension minimum build height (usually -64 in the Overworld). Strictly below, not equal. Normal death delay, effects and loot remain unchanged. Integers -2048 to 2048; scroll ±1. Right-click the apply button to restore the dimension default.
dashboard.sablelife.description_sphere_b: Charge a sphere at a fixed point ahead of the marked face, then explode once. Separate charging/blast particles and sound mixes; optional effects and block destruction.
dashboard.sablelife.sphere_blast_help: Center = marked block center + face direction × (0.55 + Start distance + Distance from start). Sphere freezes in world space when charging begins. Radius defines spherical damage; each target is hit once per explosion. Cancelling the trigger or losing the mark cancels charging. Block destruction defaults Off and uses vanilla explosion resistance when On. Preview causes no damage. Charging particles travel to the sphere center; Charging speed controls movement independently of Charge time (default 2 blocks/s). New modules use Small flame + Firework. At explosion, both the charging and explosion selections expand from the center to Blast radius at fixed 12 blocks/s. Short charges can truncate slow travel; damage radius is unchanged. At target samples the nearest eligible target within Target search range when charging begins, then fixes that world position. No Mark is required in that mode.
manual.sablelife.sphere_blast.settings:
Release position defaults Marked point; At target samples the nearest eligible target in the search range and freezes its position at charge start, with no Mark required.

Start distance clears the marked face; Distance from start places the sphere center further along that direction. Radius is spherical. Charging fixes the world point; targets can leave before the single explosion.

New modules default charging to Small flame + Firework. Charging particles move all the way toward the center at Charging speed (default 2 blocks/s). Speed does not change Charge time. The explosion ends their lifetime, so a short charge can truncate slow travel.

At explosion, selected charging and explosion particles expand from the center to the configured Blast radius at a fixed 12 blocks/s. The original damage radius is unchanged.

Charging and explosion have independent particle selections and sound mixes, with hit Effects and optional block destruction (default Off).
manual.sablelife.sphere_blast.example:
Mark the firing face. Try Start distance 0, distance 8, radius 4, charge 2 s, interval 5 s. Preview the line and sphere.

Select both particle/audio stages, then activate.

In Move set give this action enough duration to finish charging.
manual.sablelife.sphere_blast.troublesho:
Required mark loss, disabling or a falling trigger cancels pending charging. No path damage.

Only loaded destinations execute; the attack never force-loads remote terrain. Each explosion damages each eligible target once without vanilla duplicate damage.

Block destruction uses vanilla TNT resistance, not guaranteed removal of every voxel within damage radius.
dashboard.sablelife.description_slash: Fire travelling crescent blades from a marked face. Configure shape, speed, range, fan spread, angle offsets, color or particles and release sound mix.
dashboard.sablelife.slash_help: Length spans the blade sideways; width is its depth along flight. Angle offsets steer the launch; blade rotation tilts its plane. Multiple blades spread evenly across the fan centered on the offset direction. RGB defaults white. Particle mode uses the particle selection. Speed is blocks/s. Each blade hits each target once; different blades may each hit it. Terrain stops the center path; no block destruction. Sound mix begins at launch. Preview is harmless. Interval measures release-to-release time; earlier blades keep flying while later volleys launch. Trigger/mark loss stops new releases, not launched blades. Hurt Once releases one volley. Death/Release clear flight. Up to 256 blades per module; at that limit, new releases wait without deleting existing blades.
manual.sablelife.slash.settings:
Start distance and horizontal/vertical offsets determine launch. Length spans the blade; Width is its depth. Range and blocks/s speed control flight.

Count 1–16 and fan 0–180 degrees spread blades symmetrically; blade rotation tilts the slash plane.

RGB defaults white, or choose particles with size/lifetime.

Interval is release-to-release time: volleys can overlap while old blades continue flying. Release sound uses Sound mix.
manual.sablelife.slash.example:
Mark a face; try length 4, width 0.5, speed 16 blocks/s, range 24. Preview direction.

Set count 3 and fan 60 degrees for three rays; offsets change their common heading.

Add effects and select Release sound, then activate or assign to Move set.
manual.sablelife.slash.troubleshooting:
Swept hitboxes prevent fast blades skipping targets. Each blade hits each eligible target once; multiple blades can each hit it.

Launch frames freeze in world space and do not follow later body rotation. Center-path terrain stops a blade, and invisible targets behind walls are excluded; no terrain destruction.

A required mark or trigger loss stops new launches; already released blades finish flying. Hurt Once releases only one volley; death/Release clear flights.

At 256 blades per module, new launches wait for space without deleting old blades.

Sound starts at the launch position; delayed mix layers are supported.
dashboard.sablelife.rgb_help: Open the shared color picker: drag the square for saturation/brightness and the rainbow strip for hue. Precise RGB values update automatically. Confirm saves once; Presets returns to preset selection; Cancel keeps the original setting.
dashboard.sablelife.facing_collision_hel: On: terrain/body bounding boxes can block rotation, with horizontal fallback if pitch is blocked. Off: skip rotation collision checks and force turning, even while intersecting terrain. Line of sight remains a separate target selection setting.
dashboard.sablelife.pull_stop_help: Distance in blocks from the target center. Pull slows down near this distance and brakes inward movement; it does not teleport or lock the target.
module_picker.sablelife.name: Preset name
module_picker.sablelife.failed: Could not save preset (limit or file error)
module_picker.sablelife.portable: Save applied settings. Marks and module references must be set again after adding.
module_picker.sablelife.delete_help: Click twice within 2 seconds to delete the selected preset. Built-in modules cannot be deleted.
manual.sablelife.module_management.prese:
Save preset beside Delete opens a name box with Confirm and Cancel. Presets persist in the client config across worlds.

They keep applied module settings, sound layers, particles and effects; marks, arena positions and references to other modules must be assigned again.

Duplicate names receive a numeric suffix. Custom audio files must still exist on listening clients.
language_picker.sablelife.title: Select language
language_picker.sablelife.help: Switch Minecraft language now without restarting. Keep the current module and property page.
dashboard.sablelife.description_item_dis: Displays a chosen item model on a marked body point.
dashboard.sablelife.item_display_help: Copies an item without consuming it; uses its handheld model, as homing projectiles do. Base position is the marked face center, 0.55 blocks from block center. XYZ offsets and X/Y/Z rotations use the marked body axes and follow that limb. Size sets the model’s longest dimension. Always display ignores signal and life activation, but still needs an enabled module and valid mark. Empty selection shows nothing. Preview outlines its maximum size; no collision, damage or item drops.
display_item.sablelife.title: Choose displayed item
manual.sablelife.item_display.usage: Display a selected item at a marked body point. This is a cosmetic function and creates no entities, collision, damage or collectible items.
manual.sablelife.item_display.settings:
Choose the displayed item in the sample slot. It is copied with its item data, never consumed. The same handheld-model renderer as homing projectiles preserves model-based weapons.

Size controls the longest model dimension, 0.05–32 blocks. XYZ offsets use the marked body local axes, −64 to 64 blocks. X/Y/Z rotations are local degrees, −180 to 180, applied in XYZ order. The model follows its marked limb.

Always display defaults Off: enabled life activation and trigger are required. On ignores both activation and trigger, including while dormant, but still requires an enabled module and a connected valid mark. Redstone Cores can also use this cosmetic module. Preview outlines the maximum model size, not a damage hitbox.
manual.sablelife.item_display.example:
1. Add Item display and choose a sword in Displayed item.

2. Mark the intended hand face.

3. Adjust size, XYZ offset and the three rotations; Preview its extent.

4. Turn Always display On to inspect while editing, or leave it Off and activate its trigger.

5. Save preset if you want to reuse the appearance; mark again on the new body.
manual.sablelife.item_display.troublesho: No item, disabled module or lost/disconnected mark means no display, even with Always display On. Ordinary item textures remain ordinary models; this does not invent a new 3D model. Custom assets must exist on viewing clients. Unloaded bodies are not force-loaded for this feature.
dashboard.sablelife.display_hidden: Hidden: check item, mark, enable and trigger
dashboard.sablelife.move_runtime_no_targ: No eligible movement target in range
core.sablelife.name_help: Supports &0–&f colors, &l bold, &o italic, &n underline, &m strikethrough, &k obfuscated and &r reset. Example: &c&lKilling Machine. Hex: &#FF5555. Formatting counts toward the 64-character limit.
dashboard.sablelife.description_damage_a: Accumulates actual health lost and outputs a pulse whenever the damage threshold is reached. Reverse output creates a timed interruption for stagger behavior.
dashboard.sablelife.accum_help: Counts actual HP lost after part modifiers and adaptive defense. Reaching the threshold latches one pulse; excess damage and all hits during output are ignored. After the pulse ends, resets to zero and starts the next cycle. Internal channel: 0 disables, select an enabled Program internal / Program transmitter channel. Red/blue external output is independent and optional. Reverse On: normally high, interrupted for the pulse duration at threshold. Inactive modules output zero. Use a dedicated channel for stagger; other producers combine by maximum power.
manual.sablelife.damage_accumulation.set:
Threshold counts actual health lost after part modifiers and adaptive defense. Immunity and zero-damage hits do not count; healing does not subtract accumulated damage. Threshold range 1–1,000,000, default 100, scroll ±1. Pulse/interruption duration defaults to 1 second. Reaching the threshold latches exactly one pulse. Excess damage and every hit during output are ignored. After the pulse completes, reset to zero and start the next damage cycle.

Internal output uses an enabled Program internal or Program transmitter channel; channel 0 disables that destination. External Create output uses the red/blue frequency items and can operate alone or alongside internal output. Reverse Off normally outputs zero and emits configured strength at threshold. Reverse On normally outputs configured strength and goes low for the pulse duration at threshold.
manual.sablelife.damage_accumulation.exa:
1. Add Damage accumulation trigger, no mark needed.

2. Set threshold 100, channel 1, power 15 and duration 3 s. Enable Wireless channel 1 in Program internal mode.

3. Set Move set to Trigger: internal wireless, channel 1. Turn Reverse signal On on the accumulator.

4. Deal 30, 40 and 50 actual damage: one 3-second interruption begins; the extra 20 damage is discarded. Hits during that interruption do not count. After it ends, accumulation restarts at zero. When Move set loses its trigger, it cancels its current scheduling. After the signal returns it selects a move again; it does not resume the old timeline.

5. Assign red/blue frequency items if an external receiver is also needed.
manual.sablelife.damage_accumulation.tro:
Inactive triggers, disabled modules and master Off pause partial accumulation and pending output; an active pulse is ended and its cycle resets, with outputs zero. Re-enable to continue the unfinished partial count or pending output. Threshold edits reset that module counter. Reset clears accumulated damage, pending output and pulse. Death, Release and chunk unload clear temporary accumulation; presets/copies save settings only.

Use a dedicated output channel/frequency: another high producer can mask the reverse interruption. Healing cannot cancel an interruption. Damage continues to affect HP during output; only its accumulation is suspended. This module pauses Move set by signal; it does not automatically pose the body, play a stagger animation or stop already launched attacks.
dashboard.sablelife.description_signal_t: Turns the entire connected machine from six analog wireless inputs, using a marked face as front.
dashboard.sablelife.signal_turn_help: Mark a front face. Each direction selects an internal-output or external-receiver channel; 0 disables that direction. Each axis speed scales linearly with strength / 15. Opposite strengths subtract: 120 deg/s at strength 7 gives 56 deg/s. Active signal turning takes priority over Auto facing; Linear movement takes priority over both. Collision On uses the existing safe body bounds, can limit large-machine rotation and allows clear axes to continue when another is blocked. Off forces rotation at the configured analog speed.
dashboard.sablelife.turn_state_partial: Blocked axis skipped; other axes turning
color_picker.sablelife.title: Color: %s
color_picker.sablelife.help: Square: saturation and brightness. Strip: hue. Original color on the left, selected color on the right. Numeric edits move the picker; drag moves the numeric values.
manual.sablelife.signal_turn.settings:
Mark one front face. Per-axis turn speed at strength 15 defaults to 120 degrees per second, range 0–720, scroll ±5. Each of left/right, up/down and clockwise/counterclockwise roll has its own channel and choice of internal wireless output or external wireless receiver. Channel 0 disables that direction. Internal channels must provide an enabled waveform/program output; external channels must be enabled receivers.

Turn speed is proportional to signal strength: speed × strength / 15. At 120 degrees/s, 15 gives 120, 7 gives 56 and 0 stops. Opposite signals subtract on their axis: left 15 and right 7 give left 64 degrees/s. Multiple axes can rotate together; their combined rotation speed can be higher than the speed of one axis.
