manual.sablelife.signal_turn.example:
1. Add Signal turning and mark the machine front.

2. Set speed 120 and left input to internal channel 1. Enable channel 1 in Program internal mode.

3. Supply strength 7 to channel 1 to turn left at nominal 56 degrees/s; 15 gives 120.

4. Bind right to channel 2. Equal left/right strengths stop yaw; a stronger right signal turns right.

5. Configure up/down and roll only if needed, or use external receiver channels for your redstone control system.
manual.sablelife.signal_turn.troubleshoo:
Signal turning does not select or track targets. No net signal allows Auto facing to run if separately active. With net input, the first available Signal turning module controls rotation and pauses Auto facing, including when rotation is blocked. Linear movement has priority.

Collision defaults On, using contact-deflated body bounds and the existing safe rotation sweep. Large machines may be limited below nominal speed; blocked axes are skipped while clear axes continue. Off ignores those blockers. Death, disable, invalid/lost marks and master Off stop module rotation. Keep front markers, channel modes and opposing signal strengths consistent.
manual.sablelife.module_management.color:
RGB opens one shared in-game color picker for every existing module color: Mortar warning, Ground strike, Laser, Quake, both Attraction colors and Slash. Drag the square to select saturation/brightness and the rainbow strip for hue. The preview shows original on the left and new on the right.

Precise RGB expands three synchronized 0–255 fields; numeric edits also move the picker. Confirm sends one atomic update. Use presets restores the preset selector and remembers your custom color. Cancel/Escape changes nothing. Saved worlds and presets retain the same RGB values; the dashboard no longer needs three separate rows.
manual.sablelife.module_management.manua: The manual header provides Language, UI density and Back. Language switches the game resources without restarting; returning preserves the chapter, tab and search. UI density uses the same saved preference as the dashboard and adjusts text wrapping and row spacing. Right-click density to cycle backward.
manual.sablelife.server_limits.usage: These limits bound unusually large configurations. They do not change ordinary attack damage, signed part modifiers or action timing. Use the server-owned configuration when hosting multiplayer worlds.
manual.sablelife.server_limits.settings:
The world serverconfig/sablelife-server.toml controls newly authored wireless channels (default 256), particle points per player/tick (8192), loaded Sable Life projectiles per dimension (8192) and per creature (2048), shared death cleanup blocks per server tick (256), and collision checks per dimension/tick (8,388,608). Existing saved channels and their numbers are retained. Saved or already flying projectiles are not deleted to enforce a new-spawn limit.

At a collision budget limit, movement waits and reports its state; terrain blocking still stops it normally. Cosmetic emission can be reduced at the particle limit. Death cleanup is shared and rotated between pending jobs; unloaded blocks remain protected until they can be cleared.
manual.sablelife.server_limits.example: Use a modest test machine before increasing limits. Monitor server tick time and observer traffic with the actual mods and player count. Limits are not a promise of a particular TPS or supported creature count.
manual.sablelife.server_limits.troublesh: Only administrators can author or import command modules. A blueprint placement API has no player identity, so imported command modules require administrator approval through the command editor before they run. Opening and saving an ordinary module preset does not grant command permission. Editing requests and complex imports are rate-limited; retry after a short pause if a burst is rejected.
core.sablelife.deathEffectRadius_help: Lethal-hit effects use the center of the connected body. 0 automatically fits its enclosing sphere; a positive value specifies a radius up to 256 blocks. Spread adds jitter. Flash stays at the center. Delayed removal effects remain on individual blocks.
manual.sablelife.core.death_envelope:
Immediate death effects originate at the center of the connected body, including attached parts. Effect radius 0 automatically fits its enclosing sphere (up to 256 blocks); a positive value sets a fixed radius. Spread controls jitter. Burst/cloud particles start around that sphere; ring, star and spiral keep their selected shapes. Flash remains a single central flash. Sound radius is independent.

After the death delay, removal effects still appear at constituent blocks while cleanup runs in batches. Rewards keep their existing location.
manual.sablelife.core.protected_tools:
When Allow block breaking is Off, tools aimed at an activated body attack it instead of mining. Holding the button does not keep producing cracks or block-hit particles. Ordinary terrain and tool mining with Allow block breaking On keep their previous behavior.

With Epic Fight 21.17.3.1, supported native main-hand hits also charge the matching weapon innate skill by health damage actually dealt. The native skill cap, activation state and synchronization apply; the same phase cannot charge twice. Immunity yields no charge. This does not imply support for entity-only skill events or other combat mods.
core.sablelife.bossbar_color_help: Boss bar color: click forward, right-click backward. Uses the seven vanilla colors.
manual.sablelife.core.boss_colors: The Boss bar switch has a color selector beside it. Left-click cycles forward and right-click cycles backward through pink, blue, red, green, yellow, purple and white. Red remains the default for old worlds. Color persists in world saves and copied core configurations, and can be changed while alive without resetting health.
manual.sablelife.death_unloading.cleanup: Cleanup progress is saved with the world. If you leave during a large creature’s batched removal, loading the world again resumes the remaining cleanup instead of restarting the whole death or granting its reward again. Unloaded areas wait until loaded; this is different from the death-delay countdown. Removal effects remain at the blocks being cleaned.
manual.sablelife.melee.epic_guard:
With supported Epic Fight 21.17.3.1, Melee module attacks can be guarded or parried using its normal front-facing, held-weapon and skill rules. Native stamina, penalty, guard-break animation and parry timing remain in effect. The attack origin is the marked body’s world position; attacks from behind are not blocked.

A blocked contact waits for the configured Interval before trying again, without applying damage, hit effects or module knockback. Successful-hit limits are not consumed by blocks. No proxy attacker is spawned. This bridge does not change Arrow/Gun blocking or make all module attacks blockable.
arena_buffs.sablelife.title: Arena buff groups
arena_buffs.sablelife.help: All groups share Nearby player range around the living core, using horizontal distance. Alive survival players only. The Arena must be enabled, marked and triggered, with Range buffs On. Follow module needs no extra signal; internal reads the selected channel output, external reads its input. Channel 0 is unbound. Groups may overlap; strongest level wins for the same effect. Refreshes once per second for 2 seconds, then expires naturally. Existing stronger/longer potion effects are not removed. Instant effects are unavailable. Up to 16 groups / 16 effects each. Presets keep effects but require rebinding channels.
manual.sablelife.arena.range_buffs:
Range buffs defaults Off. Enable it and open Buff groups to add, reorder or delete up to 16 groups. Each group chooses up to 16 persistent effects and levels 1–5. Instant healing/damage effects are excluded. Duration is fixed at 2 seconds and refreshes once per second.

All groups share the existing Player range around the core, measured horizontally, and affect only alive survival players in the same dimension. This works while the boss is inside its Arena; the existing outside-Arena warning/return rules are unchanged. The Arena must be enabled, marked and triggered.

Follow module adds no extra signal requirement. Internal channel reads a core wireless output; External channel reads its receiver input. Channel 0 is unbound. Configure external red/blue frequencies in the core Wireless editor. Several groups can be active together; the strongest level is chosen when the same effect occurs in multiple groups.

For a half-health change, set Health phase signals for the desired health ranges, output to internal channels 1 and 2, and bind the corresponding groups. At a boundary both phases can be active if their configured ranges overlap. Signal off, leaving the range, disabling or death stops refreshes; short-lived effects expire naturally, so old/new stages may overlap briefly. No blanket removal is used on player potion effects. Saved worlds/core copies retain groups and channels; presets retain effects and control modes but require channel rebinding.
manual.sablelife.core.iron_spells:
Iron’s Spells compatibility targets the inspected Minecraft 1.21.1 / 3.16.3 release. Supported moving damage projectiles are Magic missile, Magic arrow, Small fireball, Firebolt, Icicle, Lightning lance and Blood slash, plus Fireball and Fire arrow explosions. Hitting a living body consumes the projectile, including piercing types, after one body damage calculation. Ordinary living targets keep native behavior. Explosive projectiles retain native blast damage and effects without a second TNT-formula hit.

Fire breath, Cone of cold and Poison breath use their native attack-part boxes and damage activation windows. Multiple parts touching one creature count once per window. Terrain blocks these attacks. Ray of siphoning uses the native ray and cast pulses; it heals the caster by actual body health removed. Blood slash retains its native 15% lifesteal. Part modifiers and adaptive defense still apply; fully immune bodies do not provide healing.

No proxy entities are spawned. Unknown projectile families, lock-on, chains, lightning balls and other ground waves still need explicit adapters. Burning, freezing, poison status effects and native LivingEntity-only damage/skill events are not simulated on bodies. Addons retaining a supported path can inherit it; independent paths need verification. Unverified Iron versions receive no hooks.
manual.sablelife.core.iron_areas:
Additional inspected paths: Shadow slash damages real body voxels in its impact area. Wither skull applies one full direct body hit and nearby damage; Starfall comets apply their native flat area damage; Arrow volley’s individual small arrows each damage once and stop at a body. Sunbeam retains its native 15-tick warmup and single area burst.

Earthquake, Fire fields and Poison clouds follow the native checkHits cadence, startup delay and duration. Circular areas retain the radius as well as their vertical box limits. One pulse can hit several creatures, but multiple body blocks count once per creature; hit-based radius and duration changes occur once for the entire pulse. An immune contact still counts for these native post-hit rules.

Healing areas and freeze-only fields are not converted into body damage, even when their internal amount is positive. Body damage does not simulate native poison, fire or freezing status ticks. Other area families still need verification.
arena_respawn.sablelife.requires: Requires Sable Photomancy 1.0.1 and creative operator permission.
arena_respawn.sablelife.failed: Respawn stopped. Use /sablelife_respawn cancel nearby to clear it.
arena_respawn.sablelife.error_unassemble: The core must belong to an assembled structure.
arena_respawn.sablelife.error_too_large: Template exceeds the structure or data limit.
arena_respawn.sablelife.error_unloaded: Load every connected part before recording.
arena_respawn.sablelife.error_one_heart: The template must contain exactly one life core.
dashboard.sablelife.arena_respawn_help: Requires Photomancy 1.0.1 and a creative operator. Mark the arena center, record the current connected structure and enable automatic respawn. Cooldown begins at death; unloaded spawn chunks pause it. Old cleanup must finish before native one-call restoration. Large placements may cause a brief pause. The new creature activates at full health. Record again to replace the template; clear it to stop future respawns.
manual.sablelife.arena.respawn:
Automatic respawn defaults Off and requires the inspected Sable Photomancy 1.0.1 optional API. Without it, other Sable Life features remain available and respawn controls are disabled. A creative operator records the current connected structure after marking the Arena center, then enables Automatic respawn and sets its cooldown (5–3,600 seconds, default 60; scroll ±1 second). One record per creature; record again replaces it.

The record preserves relative poses among the parts, core settings, modules, internal references and inventory. Photomancy normalizes the template around its selected basis anchor; Arena center is the placement target for that anchor, not necessarily the template bottom. Death begins the cooldown. The spawn region must be loaded; its countdown and building pause without forcing chunks. Old body and detached-part cleanup must finish first. The structure restores in one synchronous call to the native Photomancy blueprint tool placer, then a fresh creature activates at full health with new identities, valid marks and reset runtime. Every part actually rebuilt from the template is registered to the new creature, even if its connection actor is not ready yet, so later death cleanup includes all recorded parts. Multiple generations reuse the template.

Countdown and progress appear above a standable terrain surface at the Arena center X/Z, separately from spawn height. A clear surface below the anchor is preferred; if none exists, a surface above it is used. With no terrain support, display falls back to anchor height. This moves only the text, not the template. The countdown is stored in world data, independent of the deleted core. New respawns have no cross-tick construction stage; a large placement can pause the server briefly. Legacy partial builds already saved by older versions retain their incremental recovery path to avoid duplicate structures. Clear record stops future respawns without deleting the live creature. An operator within 64 blocks of the anchor or actual countdown display can use /sablelife_respawn cancel after the core is gone; it cancels the record and removes only its known partial build bodies. A failed build stops rather than repeatedly creating structures. The failure display includes the cancellation command. That command also removes orphaned copies of the same respawn display. Partial reconstructed bodies pause block-entity ticks until their complete NBT and joint commit; unrelated bodies run normally. Save/reload reinstates this guard before world ticking.

Records are server-side and excluded from GUI snapshots, presets and ordinary blueprint copies. Limits: 32 records per world/server, 32 connected parts, 131,072 blocks and 16,384 block entities by default (server arenaCaptureBlocks / arenaCaptureBlockEntities), 256 captured entities, 4,194,304 bounding-box scan cells by default (including air, adjustable with the server arenaCaptureScanVoxels budget), 32 MiB per template and 128 MiB of templates per world by default (server arenaTemplateBytes / arenaWorldTemplateBytes). A rejected capture reports the exact limit, measured value and maximum. Unallocated air chunks inside a plot bounding box are valid holes, not unloaded parts. Capture checks only allocated plot chunks and uses Sable’s native empty-chunk reads for holes without creating chunks. Independent structures outside Sable’s connected chain are not included merely because a rope is nearby. Blueprint hooks preserve supported joints and extra data; unverified third-party structures still require playtesting. Recorded inventory is restored each generation; loot duplication is intentional for an administrator-authored encounter. Native direct placement runs on the server thread; large templates or expensive addons may cause a noticeable pause. It is not a constant-latency operation.
manual.sablelife.core.iron_physical_foll:
Additional physical damage paths: Creeper mortar keeps its quadratic radius falloff; Divine smite uses its native forward box and weapon/spell damage; summoned fangs hit once at their native bite window on real ground; Ice block keeps its harmless floating phase, half-damage falling contact and cubic-falloff ground burst. A falling ice block consumed by body contact does not also burst on that same victim.

These adapters add no synthetic body entity, UUID target or entity lock-on. Native spells may retain their normal mob targeting, but the body damage paths use physical overlap, native ray positions or actual impact areas. Strict entity-targeted spells are excluded by scope. Pure freezing/poison/fire status effects still are not simulated on body voxels.
manual.sablelife.arena.respawn_notes:
Respawn placement notes: Arena center places the native template basis anchor, not its feet. Large templates can extend below this anchor. Set the anchor high enough to keep the lowest part and mounted equipment clear of terrain, and leave space around the whole template. Ground-level anchors do not automatically align the feet to ground. Terrain or other-structure overlap can cause physics push-out, sudden launches or joint strain.

Changing center after recording moves the respawn destination; the template is not automatically grounded. The ground countdown text is independent, so keeping a high spawn anchor no longer puts the timer high in the sky. Test one complete death/respawn cycle before using the encounter.
manual.sablelife.linear_movement.did_you:
Did you know? One creature runs only one Linear movement at a time, including charging. If two idle modules become eligible together, the first in the module list starts; their speeds and directions do not stack.

The other can start on a later tick only while its trigger remains active and its own cooldown permits it. A brief signal may end before it gets a turn, and an earlier continuously enabled module can keep taking precedence. This also applies when different Move sets request movement.
manual.sablelife.move_set.did_you_know:
Did you know? Within one Move set, two eligible Priority moves are resolved by move list order: the first is selected, not randomly drawn. If it is unavailable or cooling down, the next eligible Priority move can be selected.

Priority does not interrupt a running move; selection happens when the controller is ready for its next move. Weighted selection runs only when no Priority move is eligible. Separate Move sets select independently and can run together; sharing an action module does not create a second runtime instance.
manual.sablelife.core.whole_cleanup:
After the death delay, a fully loaded life whose non-air blocks all belong to its cleanup group is removed as a whole in one server tick. Mounted cannons are detached without restoring their blocks before any body is removed. Paintings and item frames attached to owned dying supports are discarded instead of being left in world space. Unloaded ownership waits without forcing chunks. Mixed ownership, ordinary world blocks or failed validation use the budgeted fallback so foreign blocks remain protected.

One whole-life attempt runs per server tick, with a maximum of 1,048,576 registered coordinates in the synchronous path. Larger groups use the fallback. Native deletion can cause a short pause for very large machines. The fallback block budget does not stagger an eligible whole-life deletion.
dashboard.sablelife.arena_record_release: Record the current structure again after every release from life.
dashboard.sablelife.runtime_trigger_soun: Signal active: listening for contact; ordinary trigger audio follows its mode
sound_timeline.sablelife.fade_help: Fade out during the final seconds within the limit; a fade longer than the limit uses the entire interval. 0 cuts off immediately. A zero limit disables fading. Does not extend a sound that ends naturally sooner.
core.sablelife.survivalInteraction_help: Off by default. Off blocks survival/adventure right-click use of living body devices and frequency changes; creative players may operate them. On allows device use; placement and breaking retain their own rules.
dashboard.sablelife.sensor_output_help: Detection radius is 1–64 blocks, default 12. A detected target supplies 15 weak redstone power into the Mark block through the selected face, so a marked redstone lamp lights up. Mark receives power; it does not emit power from all faces. Internal channel and external red/blue frequencies are simultaneous outputs. Internal 0 is unbound; enable Module output mode in the core Wireless page. Channel strength does not change Mark’s 15 power. Additional outputs follow Wireless master; a Redstone Core also stops detection when master is off. Invert applies to Mark and channel outputs: no target powers them, a target turns them off. Inversion requires an active triggered module; disable/death clears output.
wireless.sablelife.name: Name
wireless.sablelife.name_help: Name this channel (up to 40 characters). Apply with Enter or ✓. The sidebar keeps the channel number and signal state before its name. Empty clears the name; names do not change signal timing or frequency.
dashboard.sablelife.description_gyroscop: Record a preferred posture and gently restore the connected machine when it tips too far.
dashboard.sablelife.gyro_collision_note: Avoids obstacles while righting; Off may turn into terrain
dashboard.sablelife.gyro_preview_help: Cyan: world down. Orange: calibrated body-down direction. Green: allowed tilt cone.
dashboard.sablelife.gyro_help: Mark a reference part, pose the assembled machine as desired, then record its current posture as level. The chosen face need not point down. Calibration stores a local direction and survives Release, reactivation and world reload. Beyond the tilt limit it smoothly rights the connected parts; yaw is not locked. Fully level keeps recovering to level; Inside limit stops 3° within the boundary. Linear movement takes priority; recovery pauses Signal turning and Auto facing. Collision checks default On; Off ignores colliders but still requires loaded valid destinations. Re-marking or transferring the reference to a new part requires recalibration; portable presets/configuration copies also require it. Choose the main torso or a fixed reference part rather than a moving joint. It does not lift or hover; collision-safe turns on large machines may be slower than the configured rate.
manual.sablelife.gyroscope.settings: Calibration records world-down in the marked part’s local frame, so a sloped shell can define its own preferred posture. Maximum tilt defaults 20° (0–180); righting speed defaults 90°/s (0.1–720). Fully level is default; Inside limit stops 3° inside the threshold. Rotation collision checking defaults On. Physical translation and vertical-axis spin are retained during correction; yaw is not an absolute heading lock. Use a fixed main-body reference rather than a moving joint. No lift or hovering is provided; collision-safe rotation on large machines can be slower than the configured rate.
manual.sablelife.gyroscope.example:
1. Add Gyroscope and mark a reference part.

2. With the life dormant, pose the assembled machine as desired.

3. Record current posture as level.

4. Set tilt and speed, Preview, then activate. Release and world reload keep this calibration.
manual.sablelife.gyroscope.troubleshooti: Linear Movement owns the complete pose while active, so Gyroscope waits. The first recovering Gyroscope takes rotation priority even if blocked, pausing Signal turning and Auto facing; otherwise those controllers may run. Collision/budget or unloaded destinations pause correction without forcing chunks. Invalid/lost reference marks, disabled/trigger off/death or Wireless master Off stop correction. Re-marking/assembly transfer to a different reference body clears calibration; generic presets and configuration clipboard copies need fresh marking/calibration. Native copies of the same full structure keep module NBT. Large articulated machines still need practical stability testing with their motors and joints.
armor_rules.sablelife.title: Phase damage rules
armor_rules.sablelife.help: Each row applies while powered or unpowered. Unpowered mode applies until a signal arrives, pauses while powered and resumes when it ends. Unbound channels do not apply. Lowest matching modifier wins.
phase_rules.sablelife.title: Health phase rules
phase_rules.sablelife.help: Rows run independently while lower < HP% <= upper. Hold stays on in range; Enter pulses once on entry. Leaving range or losing the outer trigger cancels it. Overlaps can output together; the highest strength wins on a shared channel. Choose an enabled, configured Sequence output channel.
loot_editor.sablelife.mode_help: Chance checks each slot independently. Weighted mode draws from positive weights for the configured number of draws.
loot_editor.sablelife.edit_help: Edit quantity and chance/weight using inputs, buttons or the wheel. Shift-left raises the rule; Shift-right lowers it.
loot_editor.sablelife.template_help: Left selects; with an item, left copies the stack and right adds one. Empty-handed right removes one. Shift-left/right adjusts chance or weight. Shift-click inventory copies into the first empty sample. No items are consumed.
dashboard.sablelife.pulse_visual_help: Fixed boundary ring preserves the original style. Outward sphere expands from the release center to Radius over 0.05–10 seconds, default 0.5 seconds. Cosmetic only: damage and knockback still resolve immediately, with no extra hits during expansion. Center and wave/boundary particles can be selected separately, with size and lifetime. Empty a group to disable it. Outward particle lifetime is at least the expansion time so it reaches the boundary.
dashboard.sablelife.redstone_channel_hel: Outputs to this core's Wireless channel; 0 disables it. Enable the channel and select Sequence / internal. Uses strength, Hold/Pulse and inversion. No Mark or frequency items required; all three destinations can work together. Highest strength wins across producers. Use different input/output channels to avoid self-latching.
dashboard.sablelife.pullStrength_note: Inward speed gain per tick; higher pulls up to speed faster
dashboard.sablelife.pullSpeed_note: Caps inward speed; sideways movement is preserved
dashboard.sablelife.description_hover_an: Pin the marked block at its current position while allowing the body to swing freely.
dashboard.sablelife.hover_help: XYZ use world axes; only enabled axes are pinned. Hard pin has no offset. Elastic pin returns within the maximum offset on each enabled axis. Damping reduces elastic movement and free rotation; 0 preserves natural swinging. Enable XYZ and Lock rotation to fix the marked part’s position and posture.
manual.sablelife.hover_anchor.settings: XYZ use world axes; only enabled axes are pinned. Hard pin has no offset. Elastic pin returns within the maximum offset on each enabled axis. Damping reduces elastic movement and free rotation; 0 preserves natural swinging. Enable XYZ and Lock rotation to fix the marked part’s position and posture.
manual.sablelife.hover_anchor.example: Mark a structure block. Defaults retain the original hover: XYZ hard-pinned, free rotation, damping 0. Y alone preserves height with horizontal movement; XZ alone allows vertical movement. Elastic mode defaults to strength 20 and a 2-block limit per axis; tune for the machine. With all position axes and rotation Off and damping 0, no constraint is created.
manual.sablelife.hover_anchor.troublesho: The current world pivot and posture are captured on each activation; no calibration is needed. Off, death, lost mark or unload releases the joint; reload captures again. The first triggered anchor wins and pauses translation/pose controllers. Offset limits each enabled axis, not a spherical radius. Rotation lock applies to the marked part; bearing-connected parts may still move under their mechanical drives. Tune elasticity and damping to the machine; large articulated machines require playtesting.
dashboard.sablelife.hover_note: Mark a pivot on the structure. Activation pins its current position while leaving rotation free. Off releases it. No world calibration needed.
dashboard.sablelife.description_hit_coun: Count successful HP-damaging module hits and output an internal pulse at the threshold.
dashboard.sablelife.description_health_a: Heal or drain self HP on activation or periodically while triggered.
dashboard.sablelife.hit_counter_help: Count only actual HP loss; blocked, invulnerable, zero-damage or absorption-only hits do not count. Select a source by its sidebar number; its stable ID is retained. Interval 0 counts every damage application. Use a larger interval for continuous attacks. Output needs an enabled Sequence / internal channel. Counting pauses during the pulse, then resets; trigger Off clears the count.
dashboard.sablelife.health_adjustment_he: Positive heals; negative drains. Percent uses maximum HP. Once executes on a rising edge, or once per Move Set action window. Periodic executes immediately and repeats at the interval. Drain bypasses defenses without incoming-hit effects or hit credit; by default it leaves at least 1 HP. Lethal drain follows normal death/respawn. Healing is capped at maximum HP and cannot revive a dead life.
manual.sablelife.hit_counter.settings: Count only actual HP loss; blocked, invulnerable, zero-damage or absorption-only hits do not count. Select a source by its sidebar number; its stable ID is retained. Interval 0 counts every damage application. Use a larger interval for continuous attacks. Output needs an enabled Sequence / internal channel. Counting pauses during the pulse, then resets; trigger Off clears the count.
manual.sablelife.health_adjustment.setti: Positive heals; negative drains. Percent uses maximum HP. Once executes on a rising edge, or once per Move Set action window. Periodic executes immediately and repeats at the interval. Drain bypasses defenses without incoming-hit effects or hit credit; by default it leaves at least 1 HP. Lethal drain follows normal death/respawn. Healing is capped at maximum HP and cannot revive a dead life.
manual.sablelife.hit_counter.example: Add Hit counter: threshold 5, internal output channel 3. Enable channel 3 as Sequence / internal. Add Health adjustment: trigger internal channel 3, Once, +10 HP. Five successful HP losses then heal 10 HP.
manual.sablelife.hit_counter.troubleshoo: Covers this mod’s melee, flame, arrows, gunshots, mortar, homing shots, laser, sphere blast, slash, ground strike, quake and Area Pulse, including mechanical life targets. External native weapons such as CBC mounts lack module identity and do not count. Runtime counts are not saved; reload starts fresh. Generic presets unbind source and output. An area hit counts per target; the minimum interval is shared by the counter. Projectile direct impact and explosion count separately when each causes HP loss; later potion/burning status damage does not count.
manual.sablelife.health_adjustment.examp: Use a negative Once adjustment in Move Set as an attack cost, or a positive Periodic adjustment on a held internal channel for phase regeneration. Defaults: +10 HP, Once, Fixed HP, interval 1 second, lethal Off.
manual.sablelife.health_adjustment.troub: A core module requiring no Mark; unavailable on redstone control cores. Always + Once executes only once after activation; choose Periodic for continuous recovery. Adjustment modules execute independently in list order. Reactivation/reload resets clocks.
